chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from the one who mentioned it, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Muhammad ibn Marid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A hadith has been reported to us that you said: When you recognize (the Wilayah), then do what you will.' He said, 'I have said that.' I said, 'And even if they commit adultery, or steal, or drink wine?' He said to me, 'We are to Allah and to Him we shall return. By Allah, they have not done us justice by saying that we would be seized by the deed while it is dropped from them. I only said: When you recognize (the Wilayah), then do what you will, from little good and much, for it will be accepted from you.'

key_terms.أُخِذْنَا بِالْعَمَلِ: We are seized/judged by the deed

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'When you recognize, do what you will' in relation to good deeds and sins?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the theological debate regarding 'laxity' (Tafweed) by clarifying that 'recognition' (Ma' al-Qalb) serves as a spiritual key that guarantees the acceptance of all good deeds, regardless of their magnitude. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the notion that believers are judged solely by major sins while disbelievers escape accountability, emphasizing that true Gnosis elevates even minor acts of worship. This context highlights the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of inner conviction over mere ritualistic compliance.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from the one who mentioned it, from Ubed Bin Zurara, from Muhammad Bin Marid who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A Hadeeth has been reported to us that you<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you recognise (Al-Wilaya) so you can do whatever you so desire to’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> have said that’. I said, ‘And even if they commit adultery, or are stealing, or drinking the wine?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘We are from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and to Him<sup>azwj</sup> we are returning. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! They have not been fair to us<sup>asws</sup>, that we<sup>asws</sup> would be Seized with the deed and it has been Dropped from them? But rather, I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘When you recognise (Al-Wilayah), so do whatever you so desire to, be it from the little goodness and more, for it would be Accepted from you’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from those whom has mentioned (in his book) from ‘Ubaydah ibn Zurara from Muhammad ibn Marid who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘There is a Hadith narrated to us that you have told us: ‘When you recognize, do whatever you want.’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, I have said it.’ I then asked, ‘Can they even fornicate, steal and drink wine?’ The Imam then said to me, ‘To Allah we belong and to Him we return, by Allah they have not been fair to us. Is it fair that we will be held responsible for our deeds and they will be exempt!’ What I have said is that when you recognize, do whatever you want, that is, a little good or a great deal; they will be accepted from you.’”
